newsitem.title: UK: Gold balanced between strikes ahead of OTC expiry.
newsitem.headline: Gold balanced between strikes ahead of OTC expiry.

text.p: The gold market was balancing between two key strike prices at $350 and $355 per ounce on Tuesday, a day before the expiry of February over-the-counter (OTC) options, dealers said.
"The majority are thinking $355 calls will be exercised. But I could get friendly with $350 as well. It's very hard to say which way it's going to go," one options dealer said.
"It's more likely $355 will be the trigger but I also wouldn't be surprised if it was down to $350," said another.
Gold fixed at $353.10 on Tuesday afternoon. Prices have climbed strongly over the past two weeks after hitting a 3-3/4 year low around $336 on February 12.
Options dealers said they were doing brisk business in short term call options over the past few days, suggesting the market was more bullish than bearish in the near term.
One dealer said that a major tranche of at-the-money April call options were bought on Tuesday morning, lending the market a more positive tone.
Mid-March and mid-April were popular dates, and one dealer noted heavy interest in March 19, the date of the Comex April options expiry.
Strikes starting at $345 all the way up to $365 were commanding interest and volumes were growing.
"We've been seeing very good volumes on options starting from last week. People are nervous both on the downside and the upside," one dealer said.
Short term options, particularly one and two month dates, were attracting the most interest, with longer term dates mostly quiet, dealers said.
One month implied volatilities were quoted at 12.00 to 12.50 percent, which was off slightly from recent highs around 14 percent.
Three-months were at 10.00 to 10.50 percent, six months were around 9.20 to 9.60 percent and 12-month options were quoted at around 8.60 percent.
"There have been a supply of calls from producers and vols have been lower despite the fact that we had a $7-$8 move to the upside on gold last week," a dealer said.
"The feeling is that if the market is resilient here after bouncing from the lows, then producers who missed the opportunity to hedge might be tempted to do some hedging here."
A steady supply of options into the market would keep the pressure on volatilies, he added.
